model: sonnet (general-purpose subagent running the coordinator's security review)

findings.title: Symlinked directory in an entry path defeats the private/ignored check; symlink to .git accepted
findings.evidence: workbench_bookmarks.py:353-370 and :316-344 depend on workbench.py:209-236 _git_ignored_paths, which ignores git's exit status. A path through a symlinked directory makes git check-ignore abort with 'beyond a symbolic link' (exit 128, empty stdout), read as 'nothing ignored'. Reproduced with git 2.43.0 in a sandbox repo: with linkdir -> _private, POST entries {path:'linkdir/s.md'} returned 201 status 'present'; gitlink -> .git/HEAD also 201. Controls (_private/s.md, .git/HEAD, symlink to an ignored file, ../x, /etc/passwd, C:\x) were refused. The existing symlink test covers only a symlink to a file.
findings.consequence: Private or .git paths can be recorded in a tracked _data record and read as present, breaking the 'private files unsupported' invariant. The Vite /workbench-file route has the same fail-open and would serve the bytes. Needs a symlink already in the repo, so not web-exploitable.
findings.minimal_fix: Compute rel = resolved.relative_to(REPO_ROOT); apply _is_private_or_internal to rel and run check-ignore on [resolved] only; reject or mark excluded any entry where lexical != resolved; make the bookmark call sites treat a git check-ignore return code other than 0 or 1 as ignored; add a symlinked-directory test.

findings.title: Hostile entry paths cause HTTP 500; one bad stored entry breaks the category GET
findings.evidence: workbench_bookmarks.py:307-312 catches only PathEscapesRepositoryError. NUL in the path raises ValueError, a 5000-character path raises OSError ENAMETOOLONG, a lone surrogate raises UnicodeEncodeError in _git_ignored_paths. Reproduced: 'pub.md\u0000' returned 500; 5000 characters returned 500. resolve_entries (:331-344) runs on every GET, so a hand-edited record with such an entry fails the whole GET. No path length cap in the route or schema.
findings.consequence: Generic 500 (no leak); a category that cannot be read until the file is hand-repaired.
findings.minimal_fix: Catch (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeError) in _resolved_inside_repository (return None) and map to 400 on write; cap path length at about 1024 in normalize_entry_path and add maxLength to the schema.

findings.title: .git/_private matched case-sensitively and lexically; Windows presentation machine not covered
findings.evidence: workbench_bookmarks.py:302-304 compares only the first lexical segment exactly. The Vite route compares every segment case-insensitively with trailing dots and spaces stripped; this route does not. On a case-insensitive filesystem .GIT/config or '.git./config' passes, and git check-ignore does not flag .git. Not verifiable on Linux.
findings.consequence: A .git file can be stored and reads as present; the viewer route still refuses to serve it, so damage is limited.
findings.minimal_fix: Test every segment of the resolved repo-relative path against .git and _private after casefold() and rstrip('. '), at any depth.

findings.title: Cross-origin write protection rests on a FastAPI default; dependency floor does not guarantee it
findings.evidence: With locked FastAPI 0.141.1, cross-origin simple POSTs with text/plain, form-urlencoded and no Content-Type return 422 and create nothing; preflight from http://evil.example returns 400; PATCH and DELETE need a preflight. pyproject.toml:7 declares fastapi>=0.115, and older FastAPI releases parse a body with no Content-Type as JSON (a Blob fetch sends none). Not tested on an older release. No Origin or Host check on the backend (DNS rebinding to :8000 reaches it; existing exposure, smaller than the terminal websocket).
findings.consequence: Safe as locked. An older resolved FastAPI could allow drive-by category creation (limited damage).
findings.minimal_fix: Raise the fastapi floor to the locked release or add a router dependency returning 415 unless Content-Type is application/json on POST, PATCH and DELETE; optionally reject a mutating request whose Origin is present and not allow-listed; add a text/plain test.

findings.title: No size or count limits on bodies, entries or categories
findings.evidence: A 10 MB name was parsed before the 400. Entries per category, categories and entry path length are unbounded. Each add rewrites the whole record and each GET runs git check-ignore over all entries. create_category globs the directory twice under the global lock.
findings.consequence: A local client can bloat files and slow the single lock; loopback only, nuisance level.
findings.minimal_fix: Cap entries per category (about 500), categories (about 200) and path length (1024); reject Content-Length over about 64 KB on these routes.

findings.title: No fsync, stray temp files in a tracked directory, process-local lock
findings.evidence: _write_record (:205-220) lacks fsync before os.replace. A hard kill leaves .{id}.XXXX.tmp in _data/workbench/bookmarks/, not covered by .gitignore. _WRITE_LOCK (:93) is per process while vite.config.ts documents several backends per worktree that could share a data root.
findings.consequence: At worst one record lost or unreadable and stray untracked files; no security boundary affected.
findings.minimal_fix: fsync the temp file before os.replace; add _data/workbench/bookmarks/.*.tmp to .gitignore; document in ADR-029 that a shared data root across backends is unsupported, or use an OS file lock.
